episode.title: Claire's Brilliant Idea
intro: On Sunday, Claire proposes a weekend market at Kamo House. Local artists could sell their work. Nao could display ceramics. Leo could bring pastries with his bakery’s permission. Claire will organise decorations and posters. Emma cannot attend the planning meeting, so Claire will ask her separately about artwork.
日曜日、クレアはKamo Houseで週末マーケットを提案します。地域の作家が作品を販売できます。ナオは陶芸作品を展示できます。レオはパン屋の許可が取れたらお菓子を持ってこられます。クレアは飾り付けとポスターを担当します。エマは打ち合わせに参加できないので、クレアが作品の参加について別で確認します。
goal: I can propose an event and confirm who will help.
イベントを提案し、誰が手伝うか確認できる。
episode.warmup: What jobs would need to be shared before a small market?
words: What if we organise a market at Kamo House?
〜するのはどうでしょう（提案）。
Local artists could sell their work there.
I can display my ceramics on a table.
I will handle the posters and decorations.
Leo needs permission from his manager first.
Let’s confirm our responsibilities before we announce it.
discussion: You are Nao. Your tutor is Claire. Respond to the market proposal, offer one task, and ask who will handle another task.
あなたはナオ役です。講師はクレア役です。マーケットの提案に返事をして、作業を1つ引き受け、別の作業の担当者を尋ねましょう。
episode.followup: What should you check before announcing someone else’s participation?

rule: Use “What if we …?” or “How about + -ing” to propose. Use “could” when it is possible but not confirmed.
提案は「What if we …?」「How about ＋ -ing」を使います。可能だが未確定のときは「could」を使います。
examples: What if we organise a weekend market?
週末マーケットを開くのはどうでしょう。

rule: Offer a clear job with “I can … / I will …”. Do not assume another person will help.
「I can … / I will …」で具体的に申し出ます。他の人が手伝うと決めつけないで確認します。
examples: I can make price labels. Who will arrange the tables?
値札を作れます。テーブルは誰が並べますか。

situation: Claire shares her market idea with Nao at the planning meeting.
打ち合わせで、クレアがナオにマーケットの案を伝えます。
dialogue: Claire
What if we organise a weekend market here?
Nao
That sounds good. Local artists could sell their work.
Claire
Would you like to display your ceramics too?
Nao
Yes. I can bring cups and make clear price labels.
Claire
Great. Leo will ask his manager for permission to sell pastries.
Nao
Who will handle the posters and decorations?
Claire
I will handle them. Emma cannot join this meeting.
Nao
Could you ask Emma if she wants to contribute artwork?
Claire
Yes. I will ask her separately, and I will not assume she is free.
Nao
Perfect. Let’s confirm our responsibilities first.
questions: No. Claire will ask her separately.

choose: What if we (organise / organising) a market?
choices: What if we hold a market?
We held a market last year.
Leo has not spoken to his manager yet. What is correct?
I can prepare price labels for my cups.
Ask whether she wants to contribute artwork.

situation: You are Nao at the planning meeting. The market is planned for next Saturday, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. You can bring ceramic cups and price labels. Tables must be arranged, posters prepared, and Leo’s pastry stall needs approval from his manager.
あなたは打ち合わせに参加するナオ役です。マーケットは次の土曜日、午前10時から午後1時の予定です。あなたは陶器のカップと値札を用意できます。テーブルの配置、ポスターの準備、そしてレオの店長の許可が必要です。
task: Respond to the plan, offer two tasks, and ask Claire to confirm tables and posters. Check what is still not confirmed. Then summarise the time and responsibilities.
計画に返事をして、作業を2つ引き受け、テーブルとポスターについてクレアに確認しましょう。未確定の点も確認し、最後に時間と担当をまとめましょう。
mission.title: Confirming Jobs for the Market
lines: Nao, does next Saturday from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. work for you?
What two tasks can you take, and why?
Could you ask me who will handle the tables and who will handle the posters?
What is still not confirmed about Leo’s pastries?
Emma is not here today. How can we invite her without promising her help?
Please summarise the time and each person’s responsibilities.
mission.evidence: Tutor evidence note: The student should mention next Saturday 10 a.m.–1 p.m., offer two tasks (cups + price labels), confirm Claire handles posters/decorations, note Leo still needs manager permission, and say Emma is not confirmed because Claire will ask her separately.

topics: Which jobs need one clear person?
What should you confirm before advertising?
How can you say you are busy politely?
What questions should you ask the organiser?
How can you invite someone without assuming yes?
What details should an invitation include?
What can you say if someone is unavailable?
trivia: A stall is a small selling space at a market. “Set up a stall” means preparing that space, not opening a permanent shop.
stall はマーケットの小さな売り場です。「set up a stall」は常設の店を開くのではなく、売り場を準備するという意味です。
triviaQuestion: Does “set up a market stall” mean opening a permanent shop?
No. It means preparing a selling space at the market.
episode.closing: They plan the Saturday market from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Claire handles posters and decorations and asks Emma separately about artwork. Leo still needs his manager’s permission for the pastry stall.
